why: A cinema chain with $336-402 million of revenue, thin margins on tickets and fat ones on advertising is believable; advertising at about 18% of revenue is high for a cinema but within a factor of a few, not an impossible figure.
A business-drone market of about €380-760 million split across inspection, film and farming, with film largest today and inspection growing fastest, is believable.
A new zoo collecting 4,200 questionnaires in a month is plausible, and both pies add to 100% with the second drawn from the first's 75% segment.
A mattress market of about $23-34 billion split into spring, foam and a faster-growing hybrid segment is a believable market size and mix.

The 50 cities' $24 billion is a sensible part of the $135 billion lower-income market and the cumulative shares rise steadily to 100%; the top city at about $6.6 billion a year is concentrated but not off by a factor of ten.
Every hotel's purpose-of-stay split adds to 100%, and 62,000-224,000 guest nights at 65-82% occupancy imply city hotels of a few hundred rooms, which is believable.
All four score pies add to 100%, and 1,100 respondents being 22% of a depot's accounts implies about 5,000 accounts, plausible for a busy tool-hire depot.
Outdoor brands making 5-14 million of tent profit from 11-18 models, roughly 0.3-1.3 million per model, is believable.
Engine oil at $12-14 a litre to garages is on the high side but within a factor of two of trade prices, and orders of 25 crates against a 300-bottle discount cut-off are sensible.
Cardholders buying 23-70 drinks per half year, ordered by 2013 quintile, with lower purchases after a price rise, is believable for a coffee-shop loyalty base.
